note: The commons of the only frame in the setting where this culture can be the whole of daily life, because a three-slot world seats physical, life and qi and nothing else - the grain, the roof and the ferry are the entire content of a life here.

The whole culture is a response to a three-slot composition: no anchored season to plan against and no travel to plan for, so work is judged by what survives the year rather than by what can be moved.
They answer the levy and answer it slowly; the marshal has authority over passage and never over a body, which is the arrangement this culture is organised to survive.
The only regular material exchange this culture has, and it is in salt and seed with the counting house that answers the same requests from everybody else.
Most Commonborn are Plain Dweller and most Plain Dwellers are Commonborn - and the overlap is large enough to look like one identity, which is precisely the reading this edge refuses to make.
Field labour for seed and for the narrow line's cash, and the one arrangement on the plains both sides admit was fair.

A minority body here and a full member of the culture: a Tidecaller body cannot take the Body path and is worth more on the water than in the field, which is why it was always taken and why the commons has had to absorb the loss.
A minority body here too, and for a different reason: a dense body is a good field crew and a bad candidate for anything above realm seventeen.
A minority body that the commons keeps because its short lifespan leaves more hands than the long-lived would, and keeps at a distance because the hot ones arrive already burning.
It exists on the plains because the plains are where a household is still paying on an ascent it cannot finish, and the household that could not pay culled its own branches.
The cull is the whole cause: a line held pure inside one household concentrates faster than the same line spread across a village, and culling was the only way to stop paying for siblings.
After the seam was exhausted there was no ladder left to pay for, so the house's custom hardened around the debt it could actually still collect.
Two of this culture's households are the Quiet House, which publishes teaching against discretion and has had no line to widen since the third generation.
The house's habit of keeping its real business in one unwritten head is the same reflex as this culture's unbonded children being raised without ever being addressed.
This began as three plains households that could not pay and became a custom the households now recognise as older than their own names.
Cash and seed against field labour, renewed yearly, and the arrangement survives because neither side can afford to be rid of it.
The marshal may close the river crossings, so a house that underwrites travel is underwriting the only supply chain whose unit is a person - and it has no stake whatever in the border.
Houses on the same roads the counting house controls, and they need it: a house that cannot publish a rate cannot survive a season.
Passage is the one supply chain nobody may levy a seat on, which is exactly why consent had to be bought by somebody who was not the marshal - and the houses are that somebody.
A house that asks where a traveller was last seen is a house asking for a record, and the two roads answer the same traveller differently.
Porters carry a house's whole year on its own shoulders, so a dense body's longevity is worth more here than its strength - the reverse of every other trade on the plains.
The short-lived are the most valuable guests a road house has and the ones it is worst at losing: a furnace body that goes out on the road costs the house a customer and a creditor at once.
Pedlars and river crews keep the house's information current, and the perception-built body is paid for noticing rather than for carrying.
It is the house's own discipline: the count is kept by one member who may not write it down, taught inside four generations of the same household.
The house that holds every record on the roads cannot tolerate a house whose numbers exist nowhere, and the two are formal rivals over who may keep a record.
The clan behind it narrowed its own branches rather than marrying out of them, and a discipline that cannot be written down is very hard to extend past one household.
It is carried by a lineage that was narrowed politically and crosses races freely - the grant favours sustained effort over sudden effort, which is exactly what an unwritten count requires.
Both keep the holder of the truth in a legible form instead of a written one: a cloth grade in one, a spoken register in the other, and each is unreadable to a rival by design.
A minority body in the house and the one that notices the most, which is the qualification the office actually requires rather than the one the name suggests.

A fire-affinity body with no elemental law seated beneath it has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve, so the fastest race in the setting was the shortest-lived and the most dominant at once.
Most of this culture is furnace-bodied and none of it needs to be: what is shared is a local economy organised around heat and a declared group of the year's dead.

The plains are the only frame in the setting a fifty-year body can fill a whole year of duties in, and a place that has already lost its children to a famine has use for a custom that holds them together.
The watch and the discipline share a body and disagree about it completely: one declares the year's dead, the other teaches spending a furnace before it overflows.
Both refuse to keep a fragment of the dead, and the register's refusal to make a museum of a life spent hot is the watch's refusal in a colder climate.
Commonborn cooks, carries water and keeps the watch for a furnace body it could not become, and holds this culture without sharing its body.
The famine imposed its manners fastest on the households too young to remember the reason, and a rule learned in infancy outlives the belief that prompted it.
Both measure everything in stores and both count in public; where they part is that the mark's rules were written by a shortage and the plain's by a flood.
It borrows the household lock practice of the indebted houses: three keys where the debt culture uses three doors, on the same principle that no two may ever be out at once.
The households that keep a watch are the households that keep a mark, and the mark supplies the counting discipline the watch depends on to know how many are left.
The bodies the famine thinned were the furnace ones, but the customs it left are kept most carefully by the cold-blooded families who inherited their stores.
A water-affinity body feels the shortage least and is hardest to convince of it, which is why this culture's argument is made with locks and keys rather than with appeals.
Nothing here carries an element because elemental_law was never written in this frame, so a fire-affinity body has no budget to draw on and every discharge is paid in flesh.
It is the only culture a furnace body cannot decline: the overflow arrives whether or not anyone taught the technique - though nothing in the body asks for the discretion the tradition insists on.
They keep each other: the discipline teaches a body to spend before it overflows and the watch keeps the year's dead together for the ones that were wrong.
The discipline is taught inside the commons and takes the commons's grain as its fee, so it is a trade of a village rather than a school with a door.
Commonborn spotters and water-drinkers outnumber the furnace bodies they serve, and the ethics of the tradition belong to them rather than to the bodies it was written for.

A scar is the place a law used to be written and no longer is, and a body trained against a composition that has changed meets the difference as an injury - so the only durable art is one that is always one law short of being legible.
Seasons drift unanchored here, which is not a picturesque accident to this guild but the professional condition of its entire argument.
The lineage with no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it is this guild's founding reference, and the guild is the only body in the setting that will hold it openly.
The guild's studios stand on the plains because the plains are where the frame is thinnest and the audience for a boundary art is largest.
The studio's caretakers are plain dwellers who feed a guild that pays in food and asks for nothing legible, which is the arrangement both sides prefer.
A minority body in the guild and the one that notices a mark resolving late; the guild does not claim this and forbids members from claiming it.
Three slots buy physical, life and qi and nothing else, so spatial_law is unwritten: the ground cannot be relied on to hold a boundary, a mark or a deed - only the current and the people on it can.
A water-affinity body cannot take the Body path and was assembled for looking rather than for being hit, which makes its community the one with the most to gain from witnesses.
The river carries what the plain cannot grow and the plain carries what the river cannot hold, and both sides keep the tally in the same medium.
The banks of the mortal frame's only reliable water, where the ownership of ground is a question nobody can answer with a deed.

Both distrust the written word for the same reason and arrive at it from opposite ends: the notary writes nothing because the ground cannot keep it, the unfiled writes nothing because a list can be read.
Commonborn net-menders outnumber the affinity bodies in every river community and hold this culture, because the tally is a local custom and the water is a neighbour.
Hull crew hold the tally because a dense body survives being struck by a bank, and this community has never found a safer witness than that.
The tier's only caging ore ran out at the seam and there is no spatial law to open fresh rock, so the ladder ended and a population with bodies and no climb could only sell what it could see.
The stone shores of the mortal frame, where the only currency left after the ascent closed was knowing where not to build.
A dense slow body is the culture's craft and its customer both; the guild house that raised them is a commission and not a bloodline, which is why the craft is open to anyone.
Every part of this culture inland is the commons: the wall crews are fed, housed and counted by a village whose only standing requirement is that they come back.
A traveller's grade decides which gate a traveller opens, and only a culture that reads water every day can tell them which gate is currently the survivable one.
The guild-house that sells capacity answers a wall crew's season with a standing order, and the wall's whole labour arrangement was built around being called.
The wall crews share this culture's habit of keeping what matters unwritten: a breakwater's marks are cut once and read by the crew for generations.

A seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, so the permanent crossing failed and left a bed of unmortared seats - which is why the border is still crossed one person at a time and why its builders are the only people who make it crossable.
The guild's founding yard on the plains side of the crossing, where the work is permanent and the office is not.
A dense body is a builder's body and this guild's largest single patron is a Stoneborn clan, which is a customer relationship and not an inheritance.
Two of the guild's three founding families are plain households whose sons do not build and whose daughters do, which is how the guild survived the culls that emptied other lines.
The cultivators this guild builds for measure a threshold by whether it survives their own ascent, and the guild's practice of carving a courtesy flaw into every lintel is an answer to them.
The same guild works the shore and the gate; the craft is identical and the two commissions pay in entirely different currencies.
A border is only a problem where the two sides' compositions differ, and the Spirit Peaks is the far side of the one crossing this guild can build for.

Realms five through nine - the whole remaining mortal ladder - were closed by a limit nobody was fighting, and the people who proved the limit was a law are the reason anyone now counts instead of climbs.
The verdict established that realm nine is a limit they were never issued rather than a wall they failed to climb, and this is the only body of practice that took it at face value.
The naming handed the shortest-lived path the cheapest frame as though cheapness were its nature, and this culture is the settlement of the people who read that sentence correctly.
A realm is a band of a law value and not a rank of a person, which is the whole argument of this culture expressed as an identity rather than a claim.
Two of its three ranks came from the Second Rank settlement and hold this culture because of where they were born, not because of what they are.
The end of the ladder is why the culture counts gates instead of attempting them; a population that could still climb would have had no use for a chart.
They were the first to establish that the ceiling at realm seventeen is a composition result rather than a discipline failure, and the culture is built on that method.
Commonborn holders stop at realm eight and this culture counts eight as a spent frame rather than a wasted life - which is the reading that makes a commonest body live here.
A dense body's ceiling of seventeen is a number this culture can explain and a lower one it can exceed: it exists to make the smaller of two ceilings mean something.
A furnace body's own limit is not the frame's, and this culture is the one place the distinction is treated as central rather than as an excuse.
The permanent crossing failed and the chamber that sealed it became the only archive of why; this is the culture of that archive and its practice of reading the whole record.
The vault stands on the plains side of the crossing, on the tier whose frame is cheapest, so the effort is charged to a law value that was already low.
Both close the furnace permanently and both forbid showing off, which is the discipline's one piece of transferred ethics and its most admired.
The house's rule that nothing done inside is written down and not repeated is the register's rule arrived at from the opposite direction: too much detail, not too little.

An elemental is the first life form needing three law groups written into one body at once, and the question the register exists to hold open is whether a spirit-stone vessel is an element or an effect.
The chamber's keepers are largely watch-holders: both declare the year's dead in public and neither permits a private account.
Commonborn readers outnumber the furnace bodies in the chamber and the office does not care which, because the culture is an institution's grief rather than a body's.

Spirit stone and jade sit in the spirit tier and cannot be found below it, so cultivators walked up to the Spirit Peaks and did not come back - and the women who did not go are who the plains invented something for.

Some of this culture arrived down from the crossing rather than being born to it, which is why it admits four races in one village and why two of its standing-in households are of the Voidborn line that kept itself pure by never marrying out.
The villages that stayed behind the departing, which are the settlements whose household names outlive the people who carried them up.
It began among the commonest bodies on the tier and is held by every body on it, because a departure is not a biological event and no race has ever had one.
Affinity bodies arrived after the ascent and were admitted into standing-in households without argument; the culture asks who is present, never what they are.
A dense body's long service makes it the standing-in parent and the standing-in grandchild in the same household, which the culture considers an advantage and not a bargain.
A furnace body arrives late and leaves early, and the culture's refusal to describe a woman as waiting is what makes it usable by the short-lived as well as the long.
Every ordinary plain household is one of these and none of them would call itself that: the two ids name a people and its ordinary households, and the overlap is nearly total.
The guild is a dense body's guild and most of its members are dense, but its own register counts the non-dense majority and the two rows are kept separate on purpose.
A complete composition with no redundancy stops a maximally dense fixed body at seventeen, so the guild paid for its second ladder in the one currency its members have that a qi technique does not.
A guild that builds for the endless low construction of the mortal frame and is therefore never short of work, which is what let it fund an internal practice indefinitely.
The boundary guild took the mason guild's exposed frame as its own rule, so the practice of showing the joints spread from the yard to the gate.
The same masons build the wall and the winter hall, and the culture crosses over completely between a commission and a habit.
Commonborn apprentices outnumber dense members in the guild's own roll and the admission rite is identical, because the practice is learned in cold water and not inherited.

An unimprinted group is not weak but absent, and spatial_law absent means no process runs on size and nothing grows - so a people who cannot trust the frame chose the one sense that travels inside it.
A strained law is imprinted at the floor of its authored range and runs, and this is the one culture in the setting that performs a strained reading instead of obeying it.
The affinity built for perception rather than for being hit cannot take the Body path, which makes it the best instrument in a survey - and the guild is emphatic that it taught the rest of them.

The Still Point's held note is what a strained reading sounds like when somebody is making it on purpose, and this guild is the only culture that has taken a reading to a floor where somebody would carry a figure.
A keeper who may not write the count has the same problem as a surveyor who may not trust an eye, and the two institutions borrow their language from each other.
The grid the guild lays out and re-lays is the plains settlement pattern, because a frame that cannot report its own size needs surveying every time it is used.

A scar is where a law used to be written and no longer is, and temporal_law is unwritten here, so the clock drifts and no date is the same twice - a community whose year is two tides a day learned early to speak in water.
No process runs on an unwritten temporal group, which is the whole reason this culture has four points on a cycle instead of a calendar.
The tideline below the crossing is where a drifting clock is cheapest to survive, because nothing on a shore was ever going to keep a date.
A water-affinity body is comfortable on this shore and a fire-affinity body genuinely struggles, and both hold the culture because the tide sets one timetable for everybody.
The majority body on this shore and the one that had to be taught the register, which is recorded in the culture's own account as the origin of the custom rather than as an exception.
Dense hull crews hold this culture in numbers that would be impossible on the plains, because on a tideline the body's durability is the credential and not its cultivation.
The short-lived hold it too and the culture has never asked them to explain why, which is the strongest evidence in the setting that a culture is not an anatomy.
The one surviving settlement of the people who carried Void Serpents out of the Spirit Peaks before the caravan trade collapsed.
The same movement took these people up and, decades later, took most of them down again in a collapse; both facts are in the community's founding roll.
It supplies the settlement's own food on the terms it set when it arrived, which is the reason the community is four races and was only ever intended to be one.
A settlement that declined to price its most profitable cargo has no books to grade a traveller against, so the gate cloth is written twice by hand on arrival.
One house publishes a rate and one refuses to publish anything, and a formal price is exactly the weapon the counting house knows how to use.
The two ended up in the same reflex by opposite routes: the ledger broke on serpent values that cannot be recorded, and the unfiled broke on exclusivity nobody would renounce.
Most of the settlement is this body and none of the admission test asks what a body is - only whether a person can keep a weight honest.

Fifteen seats against six laws is the one composition in the setting with real slack, and time running ten to a hundred times faster is the mechanical content of holding a single thought longer than any civilisation has existed.
The settlement sits on the top-tier floor itself; the frame runs fast enough that the court upstairs ages a generation for every decade the floor spends, which is not an oversight but an export.
Both are transformations of the same strained reading, one measured and one performed, and the survey guild admits it has never been able to produce the floor's result.
A law imprinted at the floor of its authored range is the only thing a floor full of observers can be for, and the hum is that law read low by a hundred people at once.
The floor's one customs grade is the cloth a traveller wears, which is this culture's only answer to the requirement that every person on a regulated floor be legible.
A court keeps one door of an upper gallery and a floor keeps none, and a ledger of attendance would end the culture in a week.
The settlement's administrators are affinity bodies because upstairs is running faster and somebody has to read it twice - which is a role in a court, not an ancestry.
The counting house publishes credit, safe conduct and trading posts against exclusivity, and a community that will not accept exclusivity had to become impossible to enumerate.
Refuge on the middle paths after the caravan trade collapsed, on the ground that people who are not on any list have no use for a summit.
The exhausted seam ended the ladder, and what it ended first was the paperwork: without a core there was nothing to certify, certify or file.
They settle each other's obligations in the same material - a figure, however it is arrived at - and neither community will admit the arrangement to the other.
The keeper who may not write the count is the clearest case in the setting of a practice that is concealing a number, and this community took the practice and lost the number.
The plurality of this community, admitted on the same terms as everybody else; the culture's own doctrine is that a name is a thing you use rather than a thing you own.
Carried by affinity bodies who did not come for the arguments but for the exemption, which is the ordinary way this culture recruits.
The shortest-lived are the least enumerable and so the least listable, and this community has never once recorded a member's age.

The cost of existing rises about fortyfold per tier and only a body can be moved, so the count of who may pass became the only thing anybody could actually control - and cloth was the cheapest instrument available.
It governs the landlocked approach to the one crossing anyone can still use, which is why the marshal keeps this custom rather than overruling it.
Two of the guild house's founding households were graded cloth houses, and the culture's insistence that a credential is legible without being recorded comes from them.
The wall and the gate are the same commission: knowing which gate is currently survivable, and telling a traveller which one to walk at.
Both keep the holder's standing in a legible form instead of a written one, and both are unreadable to a rival by construction.
A charter house's cloth is issued by a livery and a traveller's room is priced by their cut; neither culture can operate without the other and both know it.
A bed of unmortared seats left a border that has to be crossed one person at a time, which is the exact problem a graded cloth solves and the reason the system exists at all.
The plurality of this culture and the body it was named for, which is precisely why the record insists the name is about land and water and not about anatomy.
The households that could not pay an ascent were commonest-bodied households, and a debt culture is a consequence of that arithmetic rather than a choice of it.
The short-lived are the worst possible debtors and the culture treats them accordingly: a furnace body is bonded earlier than any other, because the terms have to be shorter.
Most guests, most staff and most creditors on the road are this body, which is the reason the house grades cloth and never anatomy.
The plurality of the house and of the households that hold it, and a hundred-year life is exactly long enough to learn a trade and not long enough to be recorded twice.
The households that kept the marks most carefully were the ones that inherited the stores rather than burning through them, and those were the ordinary bodies.
Studio caretakers, kiln hands and the plain-dweller families that feed a guild which pays in food and asks for nothing legible.
A minority of the guild and a useful one: a furnace body sees a mark resolve at the edge of its own light sooner than anyone, and the guild forbids members from claiming that as a qualification.
The wall's labour is plain commons work - the commonest body on the shore builds the wall and eats from it, which is the whole arrangement.
The bodies that thrive on a hot shore and cannot afford a dry one, so the crew that mans a kiln-wall in high summer is mostly not this body's customers and mostly is its neighbours.
Affinity bodies read a swell the way a mason reads a wall, and this culture has never accepted the claim that this is an affinity rather than nine winters of practice.
Two of the guild's three founding households are plain families, and their building apprentices are the majority of everyone who works a gate.
Doors that must be crossed and then held closed by one person are specified against a hot body's needs as well as a dense one's, and the guild tests every lintel for both.
The bodies the register was written for, and the ones who read it aloud, because a furnace body's own account of a spent life is the only one the culture accepts without checking.
Trained from nothing and now teaching, which the guild states is the only proof that its central claim is about hearing rather than about water.
A dense body transmits ground vibration better than anything else here and is therefore the finest sounding plate in the guild, which is a use its builders never claimed for it.
The settlement's most frequent visitor and its most fragile creditor; a furnace body cannot be held past a season, so this culture refuses to hold one past one either.
Hull crews that live longer than the settlement's average stay, and a long-lived body is the only kind of person who can hold a weight honestly for a career.
Affinity bodies that came down the mountain after the collapse and were admitted without argument, and which have quietly become a third of the standing name.
A slight majority of the floor and the group the court cannot place, because a body with no registration is the one the settlement's own doctrine protects.
A minority whose own custom forbids any public rhythm, which is a smaller conflict than it sounds and is negotiated nightly at the edge of the floor.
Hull crews in numbers the roads would never have carried, and a hull crew is the easiest population in the setting to make unregisterable.

The first traveller this culture graded and the founding incident's subject: a commonest body refused entry for having the wrong anatomy rather than the wrong paper, which is why the grade is read off the cloth.
The highest-turnover holder of any grade, since a furnace body's standing expires faster than the cloth that declares it and re-dyeing is a way of life.
Gate crews, porters and the people who physically operate the doors the grades are said to open, which is the one test of a livery system nobody can fake.
Pedlars and river crews whose pass is renewed at the landing instead of the crossing, and the culture's standing argument that a different water means a different cloth.
The plurality of every threshold house on the landing and the body the practice was first worked out among; the mark says nothing about what stands in it.

The attempt to seat a seventh law consumed a vacant slot on an absence and afterwards cannot be told from an empty one, so no procedure can certify any unclaimed capacity - and a community needing certainty of welcome had to build the guarantee at the door.
A mark is renewed because an imprint is renewed, and a cut through one layer at one authored value is the whole mechanism this practice imitates at a doorway.
Layers carry their own law lists and their own share of the volume, and a household in one layer of one world is the unit whose frame can change without anyone moving.
The landing's threshold houses, whose outer rooms stay above the highest tide mark anyone has bothered to measure.
The same households cut and maintain the crossings they mark, and a builder's mark is re-cut on the evening of a death for exactly the reason a household's is.
Both use standing sound at a boundary rather than a word, and the landing's marks are re-cut whenever its frame changes rather than whenever a house changes hands.
A furnace body stands equally at the threshold and holds this culture without being asked to; a fire-affinity body and a body that cannot break a fast at all are treated identically at the door.
The affinity bodies hold it in numbers the mark's own history records as a late arrival, which is the clearest case in the setting of a practice a race adopted rather than brought.
A dense body is the culture's best evidence and not its source: the builders hold it, the houses mark it, and no household here is required to be either.
A guest-mark worn for the length of a visit and removed at the door is the same object as a guest-mark kept and never explained, and the two communities have borrowed it from each other.
